She'd been chasing the same time for two months. Changed her warm-up. Adjusted her approach. Tried a different bit.

Then Dr. Leo came out.

She didn't change a thing after that. Didn't have to.

The horse came off the pattern moving like herself again — loose, forward, finding her own rhythm through the turn.

That's what a cleared-up restriction does. It doesn't add something new. It gets out of the way of what was already there.

Dr. Leo serves North Texas and DFW performance horse owners. Mobile — he comes to your barn.

DM us to book.

It's late July. The summer hasn't slowed down — and neither has your horse.

Four months of hauling, hard ground, jackpots, and early mornings. That load adds up in the back, the pelvis, the poll. Most of it doesn't show up as lameness. It shows up as a horse that's just a little less than he was in March.

Dr. Leo is a cAVCA-certified equine chiropractor serving the DFW area and North Texas. He's mobile — comes to your barn, works around your schedule, and tells you exactly what he finds.

If your horse has been working all summer, now's the time to check him.
